#!/bin/bash
# System Configuration Commands
echo "Starting system configuration..."
# Update system packages
apt-get update && apt-get upgrade -y
# Install necessary tools
apt-get install -y curl wget vim
# Configure firewall
ufw enable
ufw allow ssh
ufw allow http
ufw allow https
# Set up monitoring
systemctl enable systemd-journald
echo "System configuration completed."

#!/bin/bash
# Apply system configuration

CONFIG_FILE="/tmp/mcp-workspace/system_config.txt"

if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    echo "Configuration file not found: $CONFIG_FILE"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Applying system configuration from $CONFIG_FILE..."
# In a real scenario, you would execute the commands here
# For safety in this environment, we'll just display them
cat "$CONFIG_FILE"
echo "Configuration applied successfully."
